title: Production Incident: Replication Lag Spike & Disk Exhaustion on Primary
realWorldScenario: At 02:00 AM, the primary database disk usage surges from 40% to 98% in two hours. Monitoring shows physical streaming replication lag to the read-replica increased from 0 bytes to 250 GB. The team suspects an unconsumed replication slot or long-running replica query.
questionStatement: Investigate the root cause of WAL retention accumulation on PostgreSQL primaries. Analyze how physical replication slots (`pg_replication_slots`), `wal_keep_size`, and long-running queries on standby (`hot_standby_feedback`) cause disk exhaustion on the primary. Provide immediate mitigation and permanent architectural safeguards.

symptoms: Primary PostgreSQL disk usage alert: 98% full
Risk of primary entering read-only panic if disk reaches 100%

candidateTasks: Identify which replication slot is retaining WAL via pg_replication_slots
Explain how max_slot_wal_keep_size prevents disk exhaustion
Execute emergency procedure to drop or invalidate stalled slot safely

expectedConcepts: Replication slot WAL retention guarantee on primary
pg_replication_slots restart_lsn and retained bytes calculation
Emergency slot drop and CHECKPOINT to free disk space
hints: Why does a primary refuse to delete WAL segments when a replication slot exists?
What PostgreSQL 13 parameter sets a maximum limit on WAL retained by a slot?
Check pg_wal_lsn_diff to calculate lag bytes.
